questions.q: The parametric representation of a point on the ellipse whose foci are $(-1,0)$ and $(7,0)$ and eccentricity $1 / 2$, is
questions.solution: Distance between two foci, $2 a e=7+1=8\therefore$ a e=4 \Rightarrow $a=8\left(\because $e=\frac{1}{2} \text { given }\right)$Now, $\begin{array}{l}$b^{2}=a^{2}  \left(1-e^{2}\right)=64\$left(1-\frac{1}{4}\right)$\\ b^{2}=48 \Rightarrow b=4 $\sqrt{3} \end{array}\therefore$ Since, the centre of the ellipse is the mid point of the line joining two foci, therefore the coordinates of the centre are $(3,0)$. $\therefore$ Its equation is $\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{8^{2}}+\frac{(y-0)^{2}}{(4 \sqrt{3})^{2}}=$1 Hence, the parametric coordinates of a point on Eq. (i) are $(3+8 \cos \theta, 4 \sqrt{3} \sin \theta)$.$

questions.q: An ellipse has foci \left(4,2\right),  \left(2,2\right)$ and it passes through the point $P  \left(2,4\right)$. The eccentricity of the ellipse is$
questions.solution:
Let, \left(4, 2\right) = {S}_{1}$ and \left(2, 2\right) = {S}_{2}$ and eccentricity of ellipse is $e$
then ${S}_{1}{S}_{2} = 2ae$ and ${PS}_{1} + {PS}_{2} = 2a$
(where $2a$ is length of major axis)
$⇒ e = \dfrac{{S}_{1}{S}_{2}}{P{S}_{1} + P{S}_{2}} = \dfrac{2}{2\sqrt{2} + 2}$
$⇒ e = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2} + 1} = \sqrt{2} - 1 = tan\dfrac{\pi}{8}$

questions.q: If the lines $2 x-y+3=0$ and $4 x+k y+3=0$ are conjugate with respect to the ellipse $5 x^2+6 y^2-15=0$, then $k$ equals
questions.solution: $2 x-y+3=0$ and $4 x+k y+3=0$ are conjugate with respect to ellipse $5 x^2+6 y^2-15=0$ We know that $a_1 x+b_1 y+c_1=0$ and $a_2 x+b_2 y+c_2=0$ are conjugate with $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b}=1$ Then, $a^2 a_1 a_2+b^2 b_1 b_2=c_1 c_2\therefore$ Here, $a_1=2, b_1=-1, c_1=3\begin{aligned} & a_2=4, b_2=k, c_2=3 \\ & a^2=\frac{15}{5}, b^2=\frac{15}{6}\end{aligned}\therefore \frac{15}{5}(2)(4)-\left(\frac{15}{6}\right)(k)=9\Rightarrow \quad k=6$

questions.q: Let $P$~be a point on the ellipse $\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1,0 < b < a .$~Let the line parallel to $y$-axis passing through $P$ meets the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2}$~at the point $Q$ such that $P$~and~$Q$~are on the same side of $x$-axis. For two positive real numbers $r$ and $s$,~find the locus of the point $R$~on~$PQ$~such that $PR: RQ = r: s$, as $P$ varies over the ellipse.
questions.solution:
Given, $\dfrac{PR}{RQ} = \dfrac{r}{s}$

$⇒$~$\dfrac{\alpha - bsin\theta}{asin\theta - \alpha} = \dfrac{r}{s}$

$⇒$~$\alphas - bsin\thetas = rasin\theta - \alphar$

$⇒$~$\alphas + \alphar = rasin\theta + bsin\theta \cdot s$

$⇒$~$\alpha \left(s + r\right) = sin\theta \left($ra + bs\right)$

$⇒$~\$alpha=\dfrac{sin\theta \left($ra + bs\right)}{r + s}$

Let the coordinate of $R$ be \left($h, k\right)$.

$⇒ h = $acos\theta

and $k = $\alpha = $\dfrac{\left(ar + bs\right)sin\theta}{r + s}$

$⇒$~cos\theta = $\dfrac{h}{a},$sin\theta = $\dfrac{k\left(r + s\right)}{ar + bs}$

On squaring and adding, we get

\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = $\dfrac{h2}{a2} + \dfrac{k^{2}\left(r + s\right)2}{\left(ar + bs\right)2}$

$⇒1 = \dfrac{h2}{a2} + \dfrac{k^{2}\left(r + s\right)2}{\left(ar + bs\right)2}$

Hence, locus of $R$ is $\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y^{2}\left(r + s\right)2}{\left(ar + bs\right)2} =1$

$

questions.q: Suppose $S$ and $S′$ are foci of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{25} + \dfrac{y^{2}}{16} = 1 .$ If $P$ is a variable point on the ellipse and if $∆$ is the area (in sq. units) of the triangle $PSS′$, then the maximum value of $∆$ is double of

Minimum value of $\dfrac{3a^{8} + 3b^{4}}{a^{4}b^{2}}∀ a, b \in R$
questions.solution:
Given , $a^{2} = 25$ and $b^{2} = 16$

$∴ e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{16}{25}} = \dfrac{3}{5}$

So, the coordinates of foci $S$ and $S^{′}$ are $( 3, 0 )$ and $( - 3, 0 )$ respectively.

Let, $P \left($5cos ⁡ $\theta,$4sin ⁡ $\theta\right) be a variable point on the ellipse.

Then, $∆ = areaof ∆ PSS^{′} = $\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}$3 & 0 & 1 \\ - 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 5cos ⁡ $\theta$& 4sin ⁡ $\theta$& 1\end{cases}\right| = 12sin ⁡ $\theta

Since the value of $sin ⁡ $\thetalies between $- 1$ and $1$

So, the maximum value of area of $∆ PSS^{′}$ is $12$ sq. units

Also, $a^{8} + b^{4} ≥ 2a^{4}b^{2} ( since, A.M ≥ G.M )$

$⇒ $\dfrac{3\left(a^{8} + b^{4}\right)}{a^{4}b^{2}} \ge$6$

$

questions.solution:
Given,& $S ( K, 0 )$ and $S^{'} ( - K, 0 ) ,$~

Now, $SS^{'} = | 2K |$ and~$PS + PS^{'} = 4$~(given)

Now for the ellipse we know that,

$PS + PS^{'} > SS^{'}$

$⇒ 4 > | 2K |$

questions.solution: Given line $2 x-3 y+4=0$ cuts the ellipse $x=3 \cos\theta, y=5 \sin \theta$. Here, $a=3, b=5$. Required equation of ellipse is $\begin{aligned}$& $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=$1 \\ & $\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{25}=$1 . . \end{aligned} Satisfy the line $3 y=2 x+4$ \$mathrm{y}=\frac{2 \mathrm{x}+4}{3}$From (i) $\begin{aligned}$& 25 \mathrm{x}^2+9 \mathrm{y}^2=225 \\ & 25 \mathrm{x}^2+9\$left(\frac{2 \mathrm{x}+4}{3}\right)^2=225 \\  \text{ and }  25 \$mathrm{x}^2+\frac{9}{9}\left($4 \mathrm{x}^2+16+16 \mathrm{x}\right)=225 \\  \text{ and }  29 \mathrm{x}^2+16 \mathrm{x}-209=0 \end{aligned} Let $\mathrm{A}$ is  \left(\mathrm{x}_1, \mathrm{y}_1\right)$ and $\mathrm{B}  \left(\mathrm{x}_2, \mathrm{y}_2\right)$ \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}_1+\mathrm{x}_2=\frac{-16}{29} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{x}_1+\mathrm{x}_2}{2}=\frac{-8}{29} \end{aligned} Here, $(\alpha, \beta)$ is the mid point of the line $\mathrm{AB}$ \alpha=\frac{-8}{29} Now, $2 x=3 y-4 \Rightarrow $x=\frac{3 y-4}{2} From (i) \begin{aligned} & \frac{25}{4}\left(16+9 y^2-24 y\right)+9 y^2=225 \\ & 225 y^2+36 y^2-600 y+400=900 \end{aligned} 261 y^2-600 y-500=0 So, $\mathrm{y}_1+\$mathrm{y}_2=\frac{600}{261} \begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{y}_1+\mathrm{y}_2}{2}=\frac{300}{261} \\ & \beta=\frac{300}{261} \end{aligned} Now, $3 \beta-2 \alpha=3 \times $\frac{300}{261}+$2 \times $\frac{8}{29} $=\frac{300}{87}+\frac{16}{29}=\frac{300+48}{87}=\frac{348}{87}=$4 So, option (b) is correct.

Given,

Equation of ellipse& $\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y^{2}}{b2} = 1$, eccentricity~$e = \dfrac{3}{2}$~and length of latusrectum~$\dfrac{2b^{2}}{a} = 1 . . . . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now we know that formula of eccentricity~$b^{2} = a^{2} \left(1 - e^{2}\right)$~so by using this we get~$\dfrac{b2}{a2} =1 - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4} . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Now by solving equation~ \left(1\right) & \left(2\right)$~we get,

$a = 2 \text{ and } b = 1$

So sum of major axis and minor axis will be~$4 + 2 = 6$.

$

questions.q: The focus and corresponding directrix of an ellipse are  \left(3,4\right)$ and $x + y - 1 = 0$ respectively. If the eccentricity of the ellipse is $\dfrac{1}{2}$, then the coordinates of the centre of the ellipse are$
questions.solution:
Let, the lengths of the semi-major axis and semi-minor axis of the ellipse are $a$ & $b$ respectively, then the distance of the focus \left(3,4\right)$ from the corresponding directrix \left(x + y - 1 = 0\right)$ is equal to $\dfrac{a}{e} - ae$
$⇒ \dfrac{a}{\dfrac{1}{2}} - a\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \left|\dfrac{3 + 4 - 1}{\sqrt{2}}\right| = 3\sqrt{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{3a}{2} = 3\sqrt{2} ⇒ a = 2\sqrt{2}$
Distance between the focus and centre $= ae = \sqrt{2}$
The slope of the axis of the ellipse is $1 = tan ⁡ \theta$
$⇒ \left($cos ⁡ $\theta,$sin ⁡ $\theta\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) or \left(- \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)
The points on the axis of the ellipse at a distance \sqrt{2} units from \left(3,4\right)$ are \left($3 $\pm $\sqrt{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right),$4 \pm $\sqrt{2} $\$left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right)$
$⇒$ Points are \left($2,3\right)$ or \left(4,5\right)$ , but the centre is \left($4,5\right)$ because it is far from the directrix as compared to \left(2,3\right)$.$

questions.q: The lines $y=2 x+\sqrt{76}$ and $2 y+x=8$ touch the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{12}=1$. If the point of intersection of these two lines lie on a circle. whose centre coincides with the centre of that ellipse, then the equation of that circle is
questions.solution:
Given, equation of tangents to the ellipse are, $\begin{aligned}$& y=2 x+$\sqrt{76} \text { and }$2 y+x=8 \Rightarrow y=-$\frac{1}{2}$x+4 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad m_1=2 $\text { and }$m_2=-- \\
& \because \quad $\text { Here, }$m_1 $\times$m_2=-1
\end{aligned} It means that the given tangents are perpendicular to each other. Thus, required circle will be the director circle to ellipse. Hence, required equation of circle is $\begin{aligned}$x²+y² & =a²+b²=16+12 \\
\Rightarrow \quad x²+y² & =28
\end{aligned}

questions.q: If $y = x + c$ touches the ellipse $3x^{2} + 4y^{2} = 12$ at the point $P,$ then the value of the length $OP$ (where $O$ is the origin) is equal to
questions.solution:
If $y = x + c$ touches $\dfrac{x^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{y^{2}}{3} = 1$

then, $c = \pm \sqrt{4\left(1\right) + 3}$

$= \pm \sqrt{7}$

Let's assume, $c = \sqrt{7}$ and $y = x + \sqrt{7}$ touches $\dfrac{x^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{y^{2}}{3} = 1$ at \left(h, k\right) .$

then, $\dfrac{xh}{4} + \dfrac{yk}{3} = 1$ is same as $y - x = \sqrt{7}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{h}{4}}{- 1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{k}{3}}{1} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{7}}$

$⇒ \left(h, k\right) = \left(- \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{7}}, \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{7}}\right) = P$

$Hence, OP = \sqrt{\dfrac{16}{7} + \dfrac{9}{7}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{7}}$ units$

questions.q: If $CP$ and $CD$ are conjugate semi-diameters of the~ellipse $\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$,~then, the locus of the mid-point of $PD$ is
questions.solution:
Let $( h, k )$ be the midpoint of $PD$.

Then,~$h = \dfrac{acos\theta - asin\theta}{2}$

$⇒ 2h = acos\theta - asin\theta$

$⇒ \dfrac{2h}{a} = cos\theta - sin\theta . . . \left(1\right)$

And,~$k = $\dfrac{bsin\theta + bcos\theta}{2}

$⇒ 2k = bsin\theta ++bcos\theta

$⇒ \dfrac{2k}{b} ==$sin\theta ++cos\theta . . . \left($2\right)$

Squaring and adding~ \left($1\right)$~and~ \left($2\right)$, we get

\dfrac{4h^{2}}{a2} + \dfrac{4k^{k}}{b2} = \l$left(cos\theta -sin\theta\right)$2 + $\l$left(sin\theta +cos\theta\right)$2$

$⇒ $\dfrac{4h^{2}}{a2} + \dfrac{4k^{2}}{b2} =$2$

$⇒ $\dfrac{h2}{a2} + \dfrac{k2}{b2} = \dfrac{1}{2}

Hence, the locus of $( h, k )$ is

\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = \dfrac{1}{2}

$

questions.q: Assertion (A): The image of $\frac{x^2}{25}+\frac{y^2}{16}=1$ in the line $x+y=10$ is $\frac{(x-10)^2}{16}+\frac{(y-10)^2}{25}=$1 $\text {. }$Reason (R): The image of a curve ' $\mathrm{C}$ ' in a line $\mathrm{L}$ is the locus of the image of every point of $\mathrm{C}$ with respect to the line $\mathrm{L}$. The correct option among the following is:
options: (A) is true, (R) is true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A)
(A) is true, (R) is true but (R) is not the correct explanation for (A)
questions.solution: Given equation of ellipse is $\frac{x^2}{25}+\frac{y^2}{16}=1$ The image of the ellipse in the line $x+y-10$ will be $\frac{(x-h)^2}{16}+\frac{(y-k)^2}{25}=1$ Centre of original equation is $(0,0)$ and other equation is $(h, k)$ Midpoint is  \left(\frac{h}{2}, \frac{k}{2}\right)$ Then, $x+y-10=0\begin{aligned}$& $\frac{h}{2}+\frac{k}{2}=$10 \\ & h+k=20 \end{aligned} Now, Given equation is perpendicular to the line joining the coordinates $(0,0) \ \text{ and } (h, k)$ So, $\frac{k}{h} \times(-1)=(-1)$ From (i), h+k=20 $\begin{aligned}$& 2 h=20 \\ & h=10 \end{aligned} Then, $k=10$ Equation of ellipse $=\frac{(x-10)^2}{16}+\frac{(y-10)^2}{25}=1$ It is obtained by the image of every point on the equation of ellipse in the line $x+y-10=0$. Therefore, reason is also true. So, option (a) is correct.$

questions.q: From the focus&  \left(- 5, 0\right)$~of the ellipse~$\dfrac{x2}{45} + \dfrac{y2}{20} = 1$, a ray of light is sent which makes an angle~$\cos^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{- 1}{5}\right)~with the positive direction of~$x-axis,& upon reaching& the ellipse surface, the ray is reflected from it. Slope of the reflected ray is$
questions.solution:
Ellipse:& $\dfrac{x2}{45} + \dfrac{y2}{20} = 1$

Foci:~ \left(\pm 5, 0\right)$

Let's~say~$\theta = \cos^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{- 1}{5}\right) ⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{- 1}{5} ⇒ tan\theta = - 2$

Now, equation of line passing~through~ \left(- 5, 0\right)$~and of slope~$- 2$~can be written as~$y = - 2 \left(x + 5\right)$or~$y = - 2x - 10$

Now, if we solve this line with given ellipse equation

\dfrac{x2}{45} + \dfrac{\left(- 2x - 10\right)2}{20} =$1$

This gives us point of intersection above~$x$-axis at~ \left(-6, 2\right)$. (Point~ \left(-3, 4\right)$~will~be rejected as slope of line joining it with focus will be~$2$~but~slope of line given is $- 2$).

Now, since~line meets the ellipse above~$x$-axis~at~ \left(-$6, 2\right)$. Therefore, it is also the point from where ray got reflected.

From reflection property of ellipse, we can say that reflected ray passes through the other focus~whose coordinates are \left(5, 0\right)$.

Hence, slope~$= \dfrac{2 - 0}{- 6 - 5} = - \dfrac{2}{11}$

$
